stem: Across the eight fMRI datasets, how did TRIBE v2's encoding accuracy compare with the optimized deep-linear FIR baseline fed the same pretrained embeddings?
choices: Significantly higher on every dataset tested
Higher only on the datasets carrying all three modalities
Comparable overall, with a gap emerging only after per-subject finetuning
Higher across cortex but lower across the subcortical regions
answer: Significantly higher on every dataset tested
label: Results · baseline comparison

stem: Why did the authors build a gradient-descent-optimized "Deep FIR" baseline on the same pretrained embeddings rather than a conventional single-subject FIR encoder?
choices: So the performance gap reflects the transformer architecture rather than input features or optimization scale
So the baseline could be trained jointly across subjects rather than one subject at a time
So the baseline would share TRIBE v2's subject-conditioned output layer and target resolution
So the comparison could be made on held-out subjects rather than held-out stimuli
answer: So the performance gap reflects the transformer architecture rather than input features or optimization scale
label: Results · baseline design

stem: How did TRIBE v2's encoding accuracy change as the hours of training data per participant from Courtois NeuroMod increased?
choices: It increased log-linearly with no plateau
It increased steeply and then saturated past roughly 100 hours per participant
It increased for cortical targets while subcortical scores stayed flat
It increased linearly until it reached the dataset's noise ceiling
answer: It increased log-linearly with no plateau
label: Results · scaling

stem: Predicting unseen subjects zero-shot, how did TRIBE v2's correlation with the group-averaged response compare with that of the individual recorded subjects?
choices: It estimated the group response more accurately than most individual subjects' own recordings
It fell just below the median individual subject but above the lowest quartile
It matched the median individual subject for speech but not for video stimuli
It surpassed individual subjects only after finetuning on held-out data
answer: It estimated the group response more accurately than most individual subjects' own recordings
label: Results · zero-shot generalization

stem: On the HCP dataset, what group-level correlation did TRIBE v2 reach, and how did it compare with the median subject's group-predictivity?
choices: Near 0.4, roughly a two-fold improvement over the median subject
Near 0.4, roughly matching the median subject
Near 0.2, roughly a two-fold improvement over the median subject
Near 0.6, roughly a four-fold improvement over the median subject
answer: Near 0.4, roughly a two-fold improvement over the median subject
label: Results · HCP group prediction

stem: What property of the HCP dataset do the authors credit for TRIBE v2's advantage over individual subjects being largest there?
choices: The best signal-to-noise ratio: the only 7T recordings, with the most repetitions per stimulus
The largest subject count of any test dataset, at 176 participants
The only test dataset providing video, audio and text for every stimulus
The only test dataset whose stimuli also appeared during training
answer: The best signal-to-noise ratio: the only 7T recordings, with the most repetitions per stimulus
label: Results · HCP group prediction

stem: After holding out half of each participant's data and finetuning TRIBE v2 for one epoch, how did it compare with a linear encoder trained from scratch on each subject?
choices: A two- to four-fold improvement in encoding score
A roughly 50% improvement in encoding score
A ten- to twenty-fold improvement in encoding score
An improvement on the video datasets, with the speech datasets unchanged
answer: A two- to four-fold improvement in encoding score
label: Results · finetuning

stem: Which category-selective areas did TRIBE v2's in-silico replication of the IBC visual localizers recover?
choices: FFA for faces, PPA for places, EBA for bodies, VWFA for written characters
FFA for faces, PPA for bodies, EBA for places, VWFA for written characters
FFA for faces and PPA for places, but neither EBA for bodies nor VWFA for characters
FFA for faces, EBA for bodies and VWFA for characters, but not PPA for places
answer: FFA for faces, PPA for places, EBA for bodies, VWFA for written characters
label: Results · in-silico vision

stem: In the in-silico replication with ten-word sentences, where did TRIBE v2's predicted response begin and how did it spread?
choices: At t=3 s in primary auditory cortex, then propagating to the whole language network
At t=3 s in Broca's area, then propagating back toward auditory cortex
At t=5 s simultaneously across the whole language network
At t=3 s in the visual word-form area, then spreading through temporal cortex
answer: At t=3 s in primary auditory cortex, then propagating to the whole language network
label: Results · in-silico language

stem: Contrasting sentences describing emotional versus physical pain, which two regions did TRIBE v2 recover in silico?
choices: The temporo-parietal junction and the middle temporal gyrus
The anterior insula and the anterior cingulate cortex
Broca's area and the primary auditory cortex
The fusiform face area and the superior temporal sulcus
answer: The temporo-parietal junction and the middle temporal gyrus
label: Results · in-silico language

stem: What did TRIBE v2 predict for the sentences-versus-word-lists and complex-versus-simple-sentences contrasts?
choices: Stronger left lateralization in both, with semantic regions for the former and syntactic regions for the latter
Stronger left lateralization in both, with syntactic regions for the former and semantic regions for the latter
Stronger right lateralization in both, with semantic regions dominating throughout
Stronger left lateralization for the former only, the latter showing no consistent asymmetry
answer: Stronger left lateralization in both, with semantic regions for the former and syntactic regions for the latter
label: Results · in-silico language

stem: Applying five-component ICA to the layer mapping TRIBE v2's latent space onto cortex, what did the components resemble?
choices: Five known functional networks: primary auditory, language, motion, default mode and visual
Five anatomical divisions: frontal, parietal, temporal, occipital and insular cortex
Five stimulus-driven components: text, audio, video and two mixed-modality maps
Five subject clusters, each dominated by one of the training datasets
answer: Five known functional networks: primary auditory, language, motion, default mode and visual
label: Results · interpretability

stem: Retraining TRIBE v2 on one modality at a time, how did the three unimodal models rank by average cortical encoding score?
choices: Video highest, then audio, with text lowest
Text highest, then audio, with video lowest
Audio highest, then video, with text lowest
The three were statistically indistinguishable
answer: Video highest, then audio, with text lowest
label: Results · multimodality

stem: In the map of which modality best encodes each cortical area, where did the text-only model dominate?
choices: The language cortices and large parts of the prefrontal lobe
The language cortices and the superior temporal lobe alone
The occipital and parietal cortices
The temporal-parietal-occipital junction and the hippocampus
answer: The language cortices and large parts of the prefrontal lobe
label: Results · multimodality

stem: Where did the multimodal encoder gain most over the best of its unimodal counterparts, and by roughly how much?
choices: Around the temporal-parietal-occipital junction, up to a 50% increase in encoding score
Around the temporal-parietal-occipital junction, up to a 10% increase in encoding score
In early visual cortex, up to a 50% increase in encoding score
In the prefrontal cortex, up to a two-fold increase in encoding score
answer: Around the temporal-parietal-occipital junction, up to a 50% increase in encoding score
label: Results · multimodality

stem: How did encoding scores across the eight subcortical regions compare with the cortical scores?
choices: More uniform and two to three times lower, yet still significant in most areas
More uniform and two to three times lower, and not significant in most areas
More variable and broadly comparable in magnitude
More uniform and roughly ten times lower, significant only in the thalamus
answer: More uniform and two to three times lower, yet still significant in most areas
label: Results · encoding performance

stem: What does modality dropout do during TRIBE v2's training, and what behaviour is it meant to produce?
choices: Zeroes each modality with probability 0.3, resampling so one remains, so predictions survive a missing modality
Zeroes each modality with probability 0.3 and reweights the loss toward the surviving modalities
Drops one modality for whole epochs in rotation, preventing co-adaptation between modalities
Drops the attention heads assigned to a modality with probability 0.3, regularizing the transformer
answer: Zeroes each modality with probability 0.3, resampling so one remains, so predictions survive a missing modality
label: Methods · modality dropout

stem: TRIBE v2 bypasses its subject block with probability 0.1 during training, routing through an "unseen subject" layer instead. What does this enable?
choices: Zero-shot prediction of group responses for subjects the model never saw
Finetuning on a new subject with an order of magnitude less data
Training jointly on datasets that do not release subject identities
Shrinking the subject block enough to fit much larger cohorts
answer: Zero-shot prediction of group responses for subjects the model never saw
label: Methods · subject dropout

stem: The video embeddings are averaged over all patch tokens. What cost do the authors attribute to that step?
choices: Positional information is discarded, expected to degrade encoding in retinotopic low-level visual areas
Positional information is discarded, expected to degrade encoding in the parietal cortex
Temporal information is discarded, expected to degrade encoding in motion-selective areas
High-spatial-frequency detail is discarded, expected to degrade encoding in the ventral stream
answer: Positional information is discarded, expected to degrade encoding in retinotopic low-level visual areas
label: Methods · video features

stem: Which shortcoming do the authors single out as more fundamental than TRIBE v2's restricted set of input modalities?
choices: The brain is modelled as a passive observer, not as an agent producing behaviour
The model is fitted to adult brains and omits neuro-developmental trajectories
fMRI's resolution prevents the model from capturing millisecond neuronal dynamics
The network's black-box character obscures the premises of its predictions
answer: The brain is modelled as a passive observer, not as an agent producing behaviour
label: Discussion · limitations

stem: When testing which cortical vertices were predicted above chance, why did the authors retain only one TR every 60 seconds?
choices: To make the samples independent despite the autocorrelation of fMRI signals
To match the 2 Hz grid on which the stimulus features were sampled
To lighten the multiple-comparison burden across 20,484 cortical vertices
To discard the hemodynamic ramp at the beginning of each stimulus block
answer: To make the samples independent despite the autocorrelation of fMRI signals
label: Methods · statistics

stem: What was the scale of the unified fMRI corpus assembled for training and testing TRIBE v2?
choices: Over 1,000 hours across 720 subjects
Over 1,000 hours across 25 subjects
Over 100 hours across 720 subjects
Over 5,000 hours across 720 subjects
answer: Over 1,000 hours across 720 subjects
label: Results · dataset scale

stem: How does the information carried by the audio embeddings differ from that in the text and video embeddings?
choices: Audio carries both past and future of the stimulus window; text and video carry only the past
Text carries both past and future of the stimulus window; audio and video carry only the past
Audio and video carry both past and future; text carries only the past
All three carry only past information, by construction
answer: Audio carries both past and future of the stimulus window; text and video carry only the past
label: Methods · feature extraction

stem: How did the architecture behind TRIBE v2 place in the Algonauts 2025 brain-prediction competition?
choices: First out of 263 teams
First out of 26 teams
Third out of 263 teams
Second out of 263 teams, behind an unpublished entry
answer: First out of 263 teams
label: Results · Algonauts 2025
